source_title: Noah Wyle Shares How He Really Feels About E.R. Costar George Clooney’s Famous Pranks - People.com
source_excerpt:
The two actors met on the set of ‘ER’ in 1993 and have remained close friends
Noah Wyle isn’t a “big pranker,” but he’s sharing what he thinks of friend George Clooney’s signature pranks
“Well, they’re funny stories to tell,” Wyle told Amy Poehler during the Oct. 27 episode of her Good Hang podcast
The two actors first met on the set of ER in 1993 and have remained friends since
George Clooney has always been a prankster, and his close friend and former ER costar Noah Wyle is sharing what he thinks about his tricks.
On the Tuesday, Oct. 27 episode of Good Hang with Amy Poehler , Wyle, 55, recalled what it was like working alongside fellow costar Eriq La Salle on the hit medical drama where he starred as Dr. John Carter alongside La Salle’s Dr. Peter Benton. The Pitt actor explained that he always loved making La Salle laugh and enjoyed goofing around with the rest of the cast.
“He has a very infectious laugh, and getting Eriq to break is one of the great joys in life,” Wyle said.
“We were all the class clowns in our class, trying to get attention,” he continued. “So the idea that we would all be serious doctors, it’s a finite concept, before we all want to start making fun of what we’re doing, especially when you’ve got George Clooney in the scene.”
Sven Arnstein/NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty
As the Emmy-winning actor shared, Clooney, 65, “really set the tone” on set. “Let’s work really hard, let’s play really hard. Let’s take this work seriously, but not take ourselves seriously,” he said, while recalling Clooney’s work ethic. “Let’s show up, be on time, be professional, erase the division between cast and crew, between foreground and background. Let’s just see if we can make this feel like a company... and I’ve taken that exact ethos and recreated it with The Pitt .”
When host Amy Poehler asked if he liked Clooney’s signature pranks , Wyle sighed and smiled.
“The answer’s no,” Poehler concluded on his behalf.
“No. Well... they’re funny stories to tell,” Wyle explained, before he went on to say that he’s “never” been a “big pranker” himself.
Wyle appeared on Good Hang to promote the third season of The Pitt , which premieres in January, and to celebrate being crowned PEOPLE’s latest Sexiest Man Alive . Speaking with PEOPLE for the inaugural issue, Wyle shared how thinks Clooney would feel about the accomplishment. Clooney has been named Sexiest Man Alive before as well, in both 1997 and 2006.
“I think he’ll be amused and feel, hopefully, like a proud papa, that I’ve come of gray-haired age,” Wyle said.
Wyle and Clooney first met on the set of ER in 1993 and have remained close friends. Earlier this year, Wyle reflected on his more than 30 years of friendship with Clooney while speaking with PEOPLE at the AARP Movies for Grownups Awards . At the ceremony, Wyle presented Clooney with the award for Best Actor in film for his role in Jay Kelly , while Clooney presented Wyle with the same award in the TV category for his work in The Pitt .
“It’s catching up when we can, but always from the point where we last left each other,” Wyle shared. “Those bonds that were forged during that show are so lovely and intimate that I feel like we don’t have to be totally present in each other’s lives to be able to have a context for each other’s lives.”
“But he’s been a real touchstone figure in my life and one who seems to pop up with great regularity at the right moments,” he added.
